mercy_translation.text:
If by the sign of the cross and faith in Christ death is trampled down, then before the judgment of truth it should be clear that no one other than Christ himself has displayed trophies and victories over death and made it weak.

If death formerly had strength and was therefore feared, but now after the Savior's coming, the death of his body, and his resurrection it is despised, then it is evident that death has been abolished and conquered by the very Christ who ascended the cross.

For when the sun rises after night and the whole region of earth is illuminated by it, there is no doubt that the sun which spreads the light everywhere is also the one that drove away darkness and enlightened all things. So too, since death has been despised and trampled down from the time of the Savior's saving manifestation in the body and the accomplishment of the cross, it is plain that the Savior himself, who appeared in the body, is the one who abolished death and daily displays trophies over it in his own disciples.

For when someone sees human beings who are weak by nature rushing forward toward death, not terrified by its corruption, not fearing descent into Hades, but challenging it with eager souls, not shrinking from tortures but, for Christ's sake, preferring the rush toward death to this present life; or when one sees men, women, and young children hastening and leaping toward death because of their devotion to Christ—who is so foolish, so unbelieving, or so hardened in mind as not to understand and reason that Christ, to whom these people bear witness, himself supplies and grants each one victory over death, weakening death in each person who has faith in him and bears the sign of the cross?

Anyone who sees a serpent being trampled down, especially if he knows its former savagery, no longer doubts that it is dead or completely weakened—unless his mind has been turned aside and even his bodily senses are unsound. And who, seeing a lion played with by children, does not understand that it is either dead or has lost all its strength?

Just as one can see with the eyes that such things are true, so when death is mocked and despised by those who believe in Christ, let no one any longer doubt or become unbelieving that death has been abolished by Christ, its corruption dissolved, and its power brought to an end.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
Athanasius continues to argue from the transformed attitude of Christians toward death.
The serpent and lion analogies emphasize that something once dangerous has been rendered powerless.
